notes: localStorage holds one key, storageKey, whose value is JSON.stringify(AppSettings) with the fields in `fields` order. load.fields: the value read back for {"<field>": <text>}. Numbers in the fixture that are not finite are written "NaN"/"Infinity"/"-Infinity". Action steps run in order on one ConfigService built as index.ts builds it, with persistSettingChanges registered. layout mirrors the settingsDialog.ts template.

text.title: Settings

search.label: Find an airfield or place
search.placeholder: ICAO, name, town, or lat, lon
search.hint: Airfields match as you type; Enter also looks up places.
search.idle: Press Enter to look up places
search.error: Place search failed, check the connection

renderScale.title: Render scale
renderScale.help: Draws the 3D view at this fraction of the screen and stretches it to full size; the HUD and cockpit displays stay sharp on top. Lower it if the frame rate is short on a large screen. 100% is off and draws at native size, supersampled for anti-aliasing where the resolution affords it unless that is switched off here.

terrainDetail.title: Terrain detail distance
terrainDetail.help: How far out terrain keeps full detail. Past it the far field is drawn coarser, which is where most of the triangles above the horizon go — lower this if the frame rate is short. The ground you are flying over is never affected. Rightmost is off.

landuseReach.title: Land-use detail reach
landuseReach.help: Only the finest terrain tiles carry the exact field, wood and town outlines. This brings those tiles in that many times further out than the terrain detail alone would, at the cost of more triangles around the aircraft. 1x is no bias.

visibleZoom.title: Finest terrain level
visibleZoom.help: The deepest zoom level of terrain tiles drawn. Each level down halves the tile resolution and drops the land-use outlines the finer tiles carry, for fewer triangles and fewer tile fetches. 12 is full detail.

landuseReveal.title: Land-use region size
landuseReveal.help: How large a field, wood or town has to be on screen before it is drawn, in pixels across. Big regions show from far away and small ones fill in as you close; lower brings the small ones in from further out, higher keeps the distance cleaner.

triangleBudget.title: Terrain triangle cap
triangleBudget.help: Ceiling on terrain triangles drawn per frame. When the view asks for more, the farthest tiles are folded into coarser ones until it fits, so a low cap shows as a coarser far field rather than coarser ground nearby. Raise it if the distance looks blocky; lower it if the frame rate is short.

farTileTextures.title: Far tile textures
farTileTextures.help: Distant ground is drawn as large facets, one colour each. With this on, those facets are painted with an image of the fields, woods and towns the detailed tiles hold, so the far view keeps its detail instead of switching it on as you close. Off shows the plain facets.
farTileTextures.toggle: Paint far tiles from the detailed ground

buildings.title: Buildings
buildings.help: Houses and other buildings from OpenStreetMap, with their roofs, where the terrain was baked with them. Far off only the larger ones are drawn, and a busy view thins them out to hold the frame rate. Where roofs were measured in aerial photos they show their real colour with the Imagery and Hybrid terrain colours.
buildings.note: Data sources and licences: see the About tab.

roads.title: Roads
roads.help: Roads are drawn as lines over the ground where the terrain was baked with them. Major keeps motorways and main roads, the ones you can see from altitude, and drops the streets, which are most of the cost over a city.

terrainColour.title: Terrain colour
terrainColour.help: Every facet is baked with both a landcover class and a satellite colour; this picks which one paints it.

landuseBlend.title: Land-use colour
landuseBlend.help: In Hybrid colour, how much of a field, wood or town is its land type's colour, and how much the terrain colour sampled from imagery.

treeDensity.title: Tree density
treeDensity.help: How many trees are placed in each wood, as a multiplier on the default spacing - 0 turns trees off. Re-grows forest already loaded, so it takes a moment to catch up over a large area.

terrainShading.title: Terrain shading
terrainShading.help: Flat colour per facet, or smoothly blended across neighbouring facets.

colours.help: Hue, saturation and brightness of the trees and shrubs, the ground, water and the sky, on top of whichever terrain colour is picked. 0° and 100% are the look as drawn; 0% saturation is grey, and hue turns every colour round the colour wheel by that many degrees.

area.title: Area
area.help: Where in the world to fly. Areas other than the home one are terrain only — no airbase, no carrier — so you start airborne over the middle of them. Changing this reloads the sim.

importTerrain.title: Import terrain
importTerrain.help: Bake a new area into the terrain, or delete one. Runs on the dev server and carries on if this dialog is closed.

text.singleArea: Only one terrain area is baked, so there is nothing to choose between.

daytime.title: Time of day
daytime.help: Local solar time. Moves the sun, so sky, terrain and aircraft silhouettes follow it. Sunrise 06:00, sunset 18:00. N flips between afternoon and midnight.

aiPilotModel.title: AI pilot model
aiPilotModel.help: Applies on the next merge / opponent spawn.

help.spawnMenuNote: Aircraft list: pick from the combobox in the spawn menu.

about.title: Data sources
about.help: The world is built from open data. Each source is clipped, resampled, measured and combined with the others when the terrain is baked, so none of it appears as published, and no publisher endorses this game.

systems.action: FCS limiter strategy (soft / predictive / smooth; FM2 only)
Import or delete terrain areas (opens the World tab)

spawn.action: Carrier barricade spawn (50 m astern of the ramp, net rigged, flying solo)

Exterior back/front of AI plane (looks at player)
Aircraft showcase (black background, orbit with numpad)
Replay the flight so far (Space pause, arrows seek and speed, or move the camera in the Free view; F4/Esc exit)
Zoom in / out (F1: padlock target, F2: lock/unlock on enemy)
